findings.citation: spec.md Goals: "A new password is held to one rule — at least 8 characters — and that same rule holds everywhere a password is set, not only here." Story 13: "the same 8-character minimum applied to the temporary password I assign".
findings.note: A fourth boundary that writes a password — creating a login for an existing Agent — keeps @NotBlank alone and accepts a 1-character password, while encoding through AgentLoginService.create like the other paths. The spec's Constraints enumerate only three DTOs, so the implementer followed the letter; the Goal says everywhere, and the human's own rationale was that there must be no asymmetry between the password you choose for yourself and the one a Manager assigns you. The orchestrator confirmed it and found the file's Javadoc now contradicts the code: it says password follows 'exactly the same rules as TesterCreateRequest's', which became false when TesterCreateRequest gained @Size.

findings.citation: No story, no ## Decisions taken entry and no ticket of this spec is the source for docs/roadmap/package-by-feature.md, docs/roadmap/README.md, the deleted docs/inbox/proposal-after-tenant-scoped-sign-in.md, or docs/agents/ticket-critic.md.
findings.note: These ride in from the branch's first commit, where the orchestrator applied the human's answers to the retro proposal. They are the loop's own bookkeeping and have nowhere else to live, because the loop never pushes main — records travel to the remote inside the next feature branch. The reviewer correctly did not flag the coding-standards rule-13 amendment in the same commit, since the spec's Decisions taken cites it by name. Answered by an (after review) entry in Decisions taken, which docs/agents/review.md permits.

The mid-feature regression fix lives in the consumer, not the shell. DialogShell still renders children unconditionally, and agent-standing-amounts-and-invoice-generation.spec.ts still selects forms by index, so the next dialog mounted in the shared shell reproduces the identical failure this branch already paid for once. No other DialogShell consumer sits in the shared shell today, so nothing is broken now.

The sign-out shape — DELETE /api/session, router.push('/login…'), router.refresh() — now exists twice, in viewer-menu.tsx and change-password-dialog.tsx. The deleted LogoutButton held the only copy; this feature turned one into two. One signOutAndRedirect(router, target) would hold it.

A local ChangePasswordError {message, field} parallels SubmitError in lib/api/errors.ts, whose own doc says it was created so the dialogs share one shape rather than three copies — the consolidation an earlier review bought. The new dialog shares only readErrorCode and adds a fourth shape.

A real inconsistency, not merely a smell: code is derived from whether ANY field error is newPassword, while message is taken from the FIRST field error. A body with a blank currentPassword and a 5-character newPassword returns {code: PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT, message: 'must not be blank'} — the dialog would mark the new-password field with the current-password's message. Derive both from the same chosen FieldError.
widthClassName is passed byte-identical to DialogShell's own default; the prop can go.
The same six-line fixture — runId, Manager sign-in, client and contract, addTester, logout, Tester sign-in — is repeated in both tests.

page.locator('[aria-haspopup="menu"]') selects by attribute rather than accessible name. Unambiguous today — ContractSwitcher is aria-haspopup='listbox' — but a second menu anywhere in the shell becomes a strict-mode failure in every caller of the shared logout helper.
